sections.name: body
sections.value:
Verdict pr:345 at 49ef44281f92522ffabd4d3ca6e1fa4e75d09ef3: PASS WITH NOTES. One round. No normal-use bug and no security exposure. Every ruling holds: spawn is the one way to create a seat (a plain spawn warns and still launches), close --stop is the one way to take a seat down, a cold seat is not woken, revive is unchanged (as_role: None), and no permission changed (may_close is unchanged; --as needs a resolved seat as creator).

Checked and holds:
- The first turn is built in spawn_role::prepare before any launch. Every refusal there returns before new_window, and the test asserts launches==1 after two refusals.
- ONE writer commit (assign_many plus the first-turns file) lands after the row write and before drop(spawn_guard) and the bind wait. The first turn is queued after the commit. A test counts one commit and one new_window.
- roll_back kills the pane by id, withdraws the watch and tombstones the row. It is one fn, used by both the failed-row-write path and the refused-commit path, and it runs once (each failure point returns). Plain spawn is unchanged apart from details.warning. A keyed resend (answer_again) never commits twice.
- close --stop: SIGTERM goes by nix::kill to the recorded pid (>1) only after proc_start matches the recorded start time, checked twice (in stoppable, then again in terminate). Never by pattern. A cold holder is sent nothing and the prime is told. A holder with no note is left open and the prime is told. The memory turn comes first.
- Paths: the role id goes through RolePaths::new, the instance through check_instance, and the seat id is memorable or check_seat_id. Commit messages carry only ids and the creator seat. A --set value must be one line.
- Cost: no loop, poll, timer or hook, and no new launch site (signal is a syscall; proc_start uses the existing site). The no-role action does in-process reads per view.
- Privacy: no paths, emails or names in the added lines.

Notes for the author (fix commits; the prime checks them):
N1 (medium). A half-written holding is possible after the commit lands. assign_many returns Err after its git commit when self.flushed() or record_assignment_committed fails (store_refusal: "committed X but could not index it"). spawn_role::commit then roll_back kills the pane and tombstones the row, but the governance branch keeps an OPEN holding and roles/<id>/first-turns/<seat>.md for a dead seat, the refusal says "rolled back", and a directory rebuild from the branch would revive that holding. Fix: roll back only for refusals from before the commit. After a landed commit, either keep the seat and return the rebuild warning, or end the holding as part of the rollback. Add a test with a store that refuses record_assignment_committed.
N2 (medium, test gap). The recycled-pid guard is untested. No test covers ProcLiveness::terminate's start-time check or stoppable's "pid now belongs to another" branch (FakeLiveness::with_recycled exists but is unused here). By inspection, deleting either check passes every test. Add a close --stop test with with_recycled (expect E-RS-NOT-STOPPED and terminated() empty) and a unit test for ProcLiveness::terminate on a start-time mismatch.
N3 (low). close --stop while a memory turn is already pending ignores --stop silently (`call.stop && pending.is_none()`), then answers the pending turn, and the process is never stopped. Refuse it, or say so in the answer.
N4 (low). A crash between the row write and the role commit leaves the seat live with no role. A keyed resend (F255 answer_again) answers ok with no role and no warning. Consider a warning in answer_again when the original request carried as_role.
N5 (low, security note). --packet reads any path the daemon's user can read (an absolute path is accepted, via caller_path) and commits it verbatim, along with --focus and --set, to the governance branch of a public repo. This is no escalation (every seat runs as the same user), but nothing warns or guards. Suggest a receipt line saying the first turn is committed to governance, and either refusing a packet outside the caller's folder or adding a simple secret-pattern check.
N6 (nit). In http/mod.rs, roll_back sits between answer_again's F255 doc comment and answer_again, so the F255 doc now heads roll_back.

Mutation: NOT RUN. Free disk is 19 GiB, below shared-build's 25 GiB floor; I neither lowered the floor nor freed space. CI rust-test passes at this head. By inspection:
(a) dropping tmux.kill in roll_back is killed by the `kill:{pane}` assertion;
(b) dropping the cold_price check is killed by "sent nothing";
(c) moving prepare after the launch is killed by launches==1;
(d) dropping the start-time check survives (N2).
No mutant is essential to this verdict. The one worth space is N2's.
